_doc: YEAR-SIM-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-21): "Have you really internalized being fully autonomous and letting yourself run for a year with no intervention? ... Don't say it, code it." A year (two, to see past the target) of the faults an unattended system meets is injected into the system's own recovery code. Each fault class has a drill in foundation/yearsim.py that runs the real function that should recover from it (the model ladder in foundation/agents.py, modelwatch successors, credwatch expiry detection, host failover, the budget governor in seed/worker/src/budget.js, the conflict resolver, the dependency and runtime loops) with the fault injected, and returns how the system behaves: recovers (capacity returns by itself), degrades (keeps running with less capacity, soft, never a stop), or fatal (nothing brings it back without a person). A drill that cannot exercise code says so (exercised false) and is never read as a pass. Monte Carlo over `runs` seeded years places stochastic faults by their yearly rate and scheduled ones on their dates; the horizon of one year is the first day release capacity stays under `fatal_floor` for `fatal_after_days`. The published number is the 10th percentile (p10). Every rate names its basis: `observed` (a measured event, with evidence) or `assumed` (a stated estimate). Strict mode assumes every identity gate (a card, a sign-in) fails on its first use. Consumers: foundation/yearsim.py (--run in .github/workflows/watchdog.yml, --check in tests/foundation/test_yearsim.py), foundation/ultrastability.py (essential variable unattended_horizon reads ops/yearsim.json), site/worker.js page /year from site/yearsim-data.js (generated).

faults.what: the hosted provider retires every model of one vendor at once
faults.basis: observed: one Workers AI retirement batch in the first month measured (doctrine/models.json, 2026-11-20); 6 a year is half that pace, since one month is a small sample

faults.what: GitHub Actions does not start jobs
faults.basis: assumed: GitHub's public status history shows an Actions incident most months

faults.what: GitHub's cron scheduler skips scheduled runs
faults.basis: observed: GitHub's scheduler fired 5 times in 1011 expected runs (AGENTS.md, AUTO-IMPROVE-1)
assumed: a few full GitHub outages a year

faults.what: Cloudflare Workers or D1 is degraded
faults.basis: assumed: a few Cloudflare incidents a year that reach Workers

faults.what: GitHub refuses Actions jobs for billing or a spending limit
faults.basis: observed: jobs refused for a failed payment on 2026-11-14 (doctrine/unattended.json actions-payment)

faults.what: the day's free AI allowance is used up
faults.basis: assumed: the governor reaches its daily allowance on busy days

faults.what: a loop's spend jumps several times over its normal rate
faults.basis: observed: an earlier fleet's D1 scans read 29.0B rows in 30 days (doctrine/cost.json findings, 2026-11-13)

faults.what: two changes collide in a generated or append-only file
faults.basis: observed: most merges touch ops/*.jsonl or generated data (scripts/resolve_generated.py, LANE-WATCH-1)

faults.what: a provider revokes or rotates a credential the loops use
faults.basis: assumed: about one forced rotation a year across the providers

faults.what: an action, npm or pip dependency is deprecated or breaks
faults.basis: assumed: actions and packages deprecate a major version every few months
